issues.description: Check name and metadata title disagree with the actual policy being enforced.
issues.detail: The file/CheckID is compute_instance_single_network_interface and the title says 'has a single network interface,' but the check emits PASS/FAIL/MANUAL on a tri-state policy that treats GKE specially and ignores zero-NIC as a non-finding. Three concerns (interface count, GKE identity, empty-interface edge) are complected into one predicate. Name the actual policy or decompose: a pure count predicate, plus a separate GKE-exception rule, plus an explicit zero-NIC handling.

issues.description: GKE exception inferred from a name prefix complects identity with policy.
issues.detail: `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` treats a string prefix as proof of GKE management. The fact 'is GKE-managed' is a property of the instance (labels, metadata.created-by, instance-group membership) — not its display name. This is place-oriented reasoning over a mutable, user-controlled field. Either capture a real `is_gke_managed` value on the Instance model from API data, or drop the exception and let MANUAL be a separate, data-driven rule.

issues.description: NetworkInterface value loses the very field that detects the public-IP risk.
issues.detail: `_get_instances` reads `accessConfigs` to set `public_ip`, then discards it when constructing `NetworkInterface`. The new value object captures name/network/subnetwork but not accessConfigs, IP ranges, or aliasIpRanges — the data most relevant to 'multiple NICs as a bridging risk.' If the model is going to exist, let it carry the facts; otherwise the next check will reach back into the raw dict again.

issues.description: Zero network interfaces silently passes with no status set.
issues.detail: The else branch sets status_extended but leaves status as the default 'PASS' from above. A VM with no interfaces is either an API anomaly or a transient state — treating it as PASS conflates 'compliant' with 'unknown.' Make the time/data semantics explicit: either INFO/MANUAL on zero, or filter such instances out before the predicate runs.

issues.description: CHANGELOG entry and PR title disagree on what shipped.
issues.detail: CHANGELOG and check directory say `compute_instance_single_network_interface`; the PR title says 'detect VMs with multiple network interfaces.' These are not the same framing — one is a positive policy, the other a negative detector. Pick one name and let the metadata, code, and changelog all say the same thing. Small, but it is exactly the kind of incidental confusion that compounds.

review.summary: The check works for the common case but complects three concerns — interface-count policy, GKE identity inference, and zero-NIC edge handling — into one branchy method, with status defaulting to PASS and the GKE exception riding on a name prefix rather than real instance facts. The new NetworkInterface value object is a step toward data-orientation but drops accessConfigs and IP data, so the model captures less than the raw dict it replaces. Naming is inconsistent across PR title, CheckID, and changelog, which is the small incidental complexity that grows. Decompose into a pure count predicate over data, a separate data-driven GKE rule, and an explicit zero-NIC policy, and let the NetworkInterface value carry the facts the check actually needs.
